summary:
I wrote $HOME/projects/llm/docs/sources.md (171 lines). It is the only file I created or changed.

What it contains, in order:
- An H1 title, the "Last verified" line and a four-sentence summary.
- An evidence-class legend with seven classes, plus how to label each one. It also gives two rules for hardware: desktop RTX 5080 numbers are not laptop numbers, and every laptop result must record the power limit.
- The primary sources, grouped as vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, NVIDIA/CUDA/host, Docker, OpenCode, model cards and quant publishers, and independent evaluations. Issue states are left to the runtime docs, which this file links to. The user's private DGX Spark runbook is described as a "measured on a different machine" source, with no path or details.
- A table of all 19 user-provided sources with the columns you asked for. Each check correction is applied in the "Independent check" column: 2 sources hold as reviewed and 17 hold with corrections.
- A section on sources to treat with caution, a five-step procedure for adding a new source (raw fetch, review, independent re-check, apply corrections, labeling rule), then Sources and Maintenance sections.

Checks I ran:
- No non-ASCII characters, so no em or en dashes and no emoji.
- One sentence per line.
- Relative links to the other knowledge base documents.

Facts that were not in the inputs and that I checked live with curl (all returned HTTP 200):
- The Docker packet-filtering doc says Docker-published ports bypass ufw.
- These URLs resolve: llama.cpp release b12418, the ghcr package page, the NGC vLLM catalog, OpenCode release v2.3.0, Ollama release v0.40.16, the Docker Hub vllm-openai tags page, discussion #15013, the TechFuelHQ companion page and BFCL.
unverified: Statement that NGC vLLM builds lag upstream vLLM releases rests on the version list in current-knowledge.md (NGC 26.10 = vLLM 0.31.0 vs upstream 0.33.0); the NGC catalog page itself was only checked for HTTP 200, not read.

Leaderboard staleness dates (SWE-bench 2026-02-26, BFCL 2026-04-12, Aider 2025-10, LiveCodeBench 2025-04, Terminal-Bench no model of 32B or less) come from the disc/sweep-leaderboards.json discovery lane and were not re-fetched.
Gemma 4 26B-A4B SWE-bench Verified 17.4 (Qwen table) vs 57.40 (NVIDIA table) conflict comes from the discovery sweep; only the NVIDIA value was confirmed by audit.json.
arena.ai returned HTTP 403, so LMArena was left out of the catalog.
kb/newcand/ was empty while I worked, so no new-candidate verification records are reflected.
OpenCode issue #50814 and llama.cpp #30118 are not linked individually; they are tracked in the topic docs.
